If the `Option<T>` is the `None`\\nvariant, `unwrap_or_else` calls the closure and returns the value returned by\\nthe closure.\\n\\nWe specify the closure expression `|| self.most_stocked()` as the argument to\\n`unwrap_or_else`. This is a closure that takes no parameters itself (if the\\nclosure had parameters, they would appear between the two vertical pipes). The\\nbody of the closure calls `self.most_stocked()`. We’re defining the closure\\nhere, and the implementation of `unwrap_or_else` will evaluate the closure\\nlater if the result is needed.\\n\\nRunning this code prints the following:\\n\\n```console\\n{{#include ../listings/ch13-functional-features/listing-13-01/output.txt}}\\n```\\n\\nOne interesting aspect here is that we’ve passed a closure that calls\\n`self.most_stocked()` on the current `Inventory` instance. The standard library\\ndidn’t need to know anything about the `Inventory` or `ShirtColor` types we\\ndefined, or the logic we want to use in this scenario. The closure captures an\\nimmutable reference to the `self` `Inventory` instance and passes it with the\\ncode we specify to the `unwrap_or_else` method. Functions, on the other hand,\\nare not able to capture their environment in this way.\\n\\n<!-- Old headings. The primary objective during training is to maintain high utilization of accelerator resources (GPUs/TPUs). From a storage perspective, this translates into sustained, large-scale data movement with predictable read pressure and periodic write amplification events.\n4\t\n5\tTraining workloads in cloud-native environments impose distinct requirements on storage systems, particularly in Kubernetes-based deployments where storage is abstracted through CSI drivers and must operate across nodes, zones, and failure domains.\n6\t\n7\t#### Key Storage Usage Patterns in Training\n8\t\n9\t- **Read-Intensive Throughput**: Training involves \"shuffling\" and streaming petabyte-scale datasets (images, text tokens, or sensor logs) across hundreds of distributed nodes. Storage must support high-bandwidth, parallel access to prevent the \"I/O Wait\" bottleneck, where GPUs sit idle waiting for the next batch of data.\n10\t\n11\t- **Checkpointing and Resumeability (Write-Burstiness)**: Distributed training is prone to hardware failures or preemption (e.g., using Spot instances). To mitigate loss, the system periodically saves the entire model state (checkpoints) to persistent storage. This creates massive, synchronized write bursts across the cluster, requiring storage backends with high aggregate write performance and metadata stability.\n12\t\n13\t- **Randomized Data Access and Shuffling**: To improve model generalization, training pipelines typically shuffle data and perform pseudo-random access across datasets. This disrupts sequential read optimizations and produces high fan-out random read patterns. Storage systems must tolerate non-sequential access, high IOPS across distributed workers, concurrent metadata lookups. Cloud-native storage solutions often use distributed file systems (parallel FS) or specialized CSI drivers with local NVMe caching to provide the low-latency random seeks required for diverse data loaders.\n14\t\n15\t- **Metadata Overhead**: Training datasets often consist of millions of small files (e.g., individual JPEGs or JSON snippets). This puts immense pressure on the storage metadata server. Architectures often move toward \"containerized\" data formats like TFRecord, WebDataset, or Parquet to aggregate small files into larger, more manageable chunks, reducing metadata operations.\n16\t\n17\t- **Data Versioning and Lineage**: Reproducibility is a core tenet of MLOps. Storage must support immutable snapshots or integration with versioning tools to ensure that the exact dataset used for a specific training run can be audited or retrained in the future.\n18\t\n19\t- **Scratch Space and Intermediate State**: During the training process, temporary data such as shuffled buffers or gradients are often stored in \"scratch\" space. This requires high-speed, ephemeral storage, often HostPath or Local Persistent Volumes (PVs), to minimize the latency of intermediate calculations.\n20\t\n21\t#### References\n22\t\n23\t**Data Formats:**\n24\t- [Apache Parquet - Columnar Storage Format](https://parquet.apache.org/)\n25\t- [TFRecord - TensorFlow Data Format](https://www.tensorflow.org/tutorials/load_data/tfrecord)\n26\t- [WebDataset - High-Performance Data Loading for PyTorch](https://github.com/webdataset/webdataset)\n27\t\n28\t**Training Frameworks:**\n29\t- [PyTorch - Deep Learning Framework](https://pytorch.org/)\n30\t- [TensorFlow - End-to-End ML Platform](https://www.tensorflow.org/)\n31\t- [DeepSpeed - Deep Learning Optimization Library](https://www.deepspeed.ai/)\n32\t- [Horovod - Distributed Training Framework](https://horovod.readthedocs.io/)\n33\t\n34\t**Data Versioning & MLOps:**\n35\t- [DVC (Data Version Control) - ML Experiment Management](https://dvc.org/)\n36\t- [Kubeflow Training Operator - Distributed Training on Kubernetes](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/trainer/)\n37\t- [Ray Data - Scalable Data Processing for AI](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/data/data.html)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"817c6579-29d9-4984-ac11-c3015ed21312","uuid":"37685f1a-f8d4-4fa2-a19d-3c5aa5c673f7","timestamp":"2026-10-14T08:13:52.374Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/work/packets/03469558b145266d/before.md","content":"### Training and its Storage Usage Patterns\n\nUnlike inference workloads, which are predominantly request–response and latency-sensitive, model training is a long-running, distributed, throughput-oriented workload. Storage systems must tolerate non-sequential access, high IOPS across distributed workers, concurrent metadata lookups. Cloud-native storage solutions often use distributed file systems (parallel FS) or specialized CSI drivers with local NVMe caching to provide the low-latency random seeks required for diverse data loaders.\n\n- **Metadata Overhead**: Training datasets often consist of millions of small files (e.g., individual JPEGs or JSON snippets). A quota will only measure usage for a resource if it matches\\nthe intersection of enumerated scopes.\\n\\nWhen a scope is added to the quota, it limits the number of resources it supports to those that pertain to the scope.\\nResources specified on the quota outside of the allowed set results in a validation error.\\n\\nKubernetes {{< skew currentVersion >}} supports the following scopes:\\n\\n| Scope | Description |\\n| ----- | ----------- |\\n| [`BestEffort`](#quota-scope-best-effort) | Match pods that have best effort quality of service. |\\n| [`CrossNamespacePodAffinity`](#cross-namespace-pod-affinity-scope) | Match pods that have cross-namespace pod [(anti)affinity terms](/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node). |\\n| [`NotBestEffort`](#quota-scope-non-best-effort) | Match pods that do not have best effort quality of service. |\\n| [`NotTerminating`](#quota-scope-non-terminating) | Match pods where `.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds`]() is `nil`]() |\\n| [`PriorityClass`](#resource-quota-per-priorityclass) | Match pods that references the specified [priority class](/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/pod-priority-preemption). |\\n| [`Terminating`](#quota-scope-terminating) | Match pods where `.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds`]() >= `0`]() |\\n| [`VolumeAttributesClass`](#quota-scope-volume-attributes-class) | Match PersistentVolumeClaims that reference the specified [volume attributes class](/docs/concepts/storage/volume-attributes-classes). |\\n\\nResourceQuotas with a scope set can also have a optional `scopeSelector` field. You define one or more _match expressions_\\nthat specify an `operators` and, if relevant, a set of `values` to match. For example:\\n\\n```yaml\\n  scopeSelector:\\n    matchExpressions:\\n      - scopeName: BestEffort # Match pods that have best effort quality of service\\n        operator: Exists # optional; \\\"Exists\\\" is implied for BestEffort scope\\n```\\n\\nThe `scopeSelector` supports the following values in the `operator` field:\\n\\n* `In`\\n* `NotIn`\\n* `Exists`\\n* `DoesNotExist`\\n\\nIf the `operator` is `In` or `NotIn`, the `values` field must have at least\\none value. For example:\\n\\n```yaml\\n  scopeSelector:\\n    matchExpressions:\\n      - scopeName: PriorityClass\\n        operator: In\\n        values:\\n          - middle\\n```\\n\\nIf the `operator` is `Exists` or `DoesNotExist`, the `values` field must *NOT* be\\nspecified.\\n\\n### Best effort Pods scope {#quota-scope-best-effort}\\n\\nThis scope only tracks quota consumed by Pods.\\nIt only matches pods that have the [best effort](/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-qos/#besteffort)\\n[QoS class](/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-qos/).\\n\\nThe `operator` for a `scopeSelector` must be `Exists`.\\n\\n### Not-best-effort Pods scope {#quota-scope-non-best-effort}\\n\\nThis scope only tracks quota consumed by Pods.\\nIt only matches pods that have the [Guaranteed](/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-qos/#guaranteed)\\nor [Burstable](/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-qos/#burstable)\\n[QoS class](/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-qos/).\\n\\nThe `operator` for a `scopeSelector` must be `Exists`.\\n\\n### Non-terminating Pods scope {#quota-scope-non-terminating}\\n\\nThis scope only tracks quota consumed by Pods that are not terminating. The `operator` for a `scopeSelector`\\nmust be `Exists`.\\n\\nA Pod is not terminating if the `.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds` field is unset.\\n\\nYou can use a ResourceQuota with this scope to manage the following resources:\\n\\n* `count.pods`\\n* `pods`\\n* `cpu`\\n* `memory`\\n* `requests.cpu`\\n* `requests.memory`\\n* `limits.cpu`\\n* `limits.memory`\\n\\n### Terminating Pods scope {#quota-scope-terminating}\\n\\nThis scope only tracks quota consumed by Pods that are terminating. The `operator` for a `scopeSelector`\\nmust be `Exists`.\\n\\nA Pod is considered as _terminating_ if the `.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds` field is set to any number.\\n\\nYou can use a ResourceQuota with this scope to manage the following resources:\\n\\n* `count.pods`\\n* `pods`\\n* `cpu`\\n* `memory`\\n* `requests.cpu`\\n* `requests.memory`\\n* `limits.cpu`\\n* `limits.memory`\\n\\n### Cross-namespace pod affinity scope\\n \\n{{< feature-state for_k8s_version=\\\"v1.24\\\" state=\\\"stable\\\" >}}\\n\\nYou can use `CrossNamespacePodAffinity` [quota scope](#quota-scopes) to limit which namespaces are allowed to\\nhave pods with affinity terms that cross namespaces. Specifically, it controls which pods are allowed\\nto set `namespaces` or `namespaceSelector` fields in pod [(anti)affinity terms](/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node).\\n\\nPreventing users from using cross-namespace affinity terms might be desired since a pod\\nwith anti-affinity constraints can block pods from all other namespaces\\nfrom getting scheduled in a failure domain.\\n\\nUsing this scope, you (as a cluster administrator) can prevent certain namespaces - such as `foo-ns` in the example below -\\nfrom having pods that use cross-namespace pod affinity. unchanged.\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl describe quota\\n```\\n\\n```\\nName:       pods-high\\nNamespace:  default\\nResource    Used  Hard\\n--------    ----  ----\\ncpu         500m  1k\\nmemory Limiting PriorityClass consumption by default\\n\\nIt may be desired that pods at a particular priority, such as \\\"cluster-services\\\",\\nshould be allowed in a namespace, if and only if, a matching quota object exists.\\n\\nWith this mechanism, operators are able to restrict usage of certain high\\npriority classes to a limited number of namespaces and not every namespace\\nwill be able to consume these priority classes by default.\\n\\nTo enforce this, `kube-apiserver` flag `--admission-control-config-file` should be\\nused to pass path to the following configuration file:\\n\\n```yaml\\napiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1\\nkind: AdmissionConfiguration\\nplugins:\\n- name: \\\"ResourceQuota\\\"\\n  configuration:\\n    apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1\\n    kind: ResourceQuotaConfiguration\\n    limitedResources:\\n    - resource: pods\\n      matchScopes:\\n      - scopeName: PriorityClass\\n        operator: In\\n        values: [\\\"cluster-services\\\"]\\n```\\n\\nThen, create a resource quota object in the `kube-system` namespace:\\n\\n{{% code_sample file=\\\"policy/priority-class-resourcequota.yaml\\\" %}}\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl apply -f https://k8s.io/examples/policy/priority-class-resourcequota.yaml -n kube-system\\n```\\n\\n```none\\nresourcequota/pods-cluster-services created\\n```\\n\\nIn this case, a pod creation will be allowed if:\\n\\n1. the Pod's `priorityClassName` is not specified.\\n1. the Pod's `priorityClassName` is specified to a value other than `cluster-services`.\\n1. the Pod's `priorityClassName` is set to `cluster-services`, it is to be created\\n   in the `kube-system` namespace, and it has passed the resource quota check.\\n\\nA Pod creation request is rejected if its `priorityClassName` is set to `cluster-services`\\nand it is to be created in a namespace other than `kube-system`.\\n\\n### VolumeAttributesClass scope {#quota-scope-volume-attributes-class}\\n\\n{{< feature-state feature_gate_name=\\\"VolumeAttributesClass\\\" >}}\\n\\nThis scope only tracks quota consumed by creation.\\nYou can control a PVC's consumption of storage resources based on the associated\\nVolumeAttributesClasses, by using the `scopeSelector` field in the quota spec.\\n\\nThe PVC references により定期的に実行されるコンテナの診断です。診断を行うために、kubeletはコンテナ内でコードを実行するか、ネットワークリクエストします。\\n\\n### チェックのメカニズム {#probe-check-methods}\\n\\nprobeを使ってコンテナをチェックする4つの異なる方法があります。\\n各probeは、この4つの仕組みのうち1つを正確に定義する必要があります:\\n\\n`exec`\\n: コンテナ内で特定のコマンドを実行します。コマンドがステータス0で終了した場合に診断を成功と見なします。\\n\\n`grpc`\\n: [gRPC](https://grpc.io/)を使ってリモートプロシージャコールを実行します。\\n  ターゲットは、[gRPC health checks](https://grpc.io/grpc/core/md_doc_health-checking.html)を実装する必要があります。\\n  レスポンスの`status`が`SERVING`の場合に診断を成功と見なします。\\n  gRPCはアルファ版の機能のため、`GRPCContainerProbe`[フィーチャーゲート](/ja/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/feature-gates/)が\\n  有効の場合のみ利用可能です。\\n\\n`httpGet`\\n: PodのIPアドレスに対して、指定されたポートとパスでHTTP `GET`のリクエストを送信します。\\n  レスポンスのステータスコードが200以上400未満の際に診断を成功とみなします。\\n\\n`tcpSocket`\\n: PodのIPアドレスに対して、指定されたポートでTCPチェックを行います。\\n  そのポートが空いていれば診断を成功とみなします。\\n  オープンしてすぐにリモートシステム(コンテナ)が接続を切断した場合、健全な状態としてカウントします。\\n\\n### Probeの結果 {#probe-outcome}\\n\\n各Probe 次の3つのうちの一つの結果を持ちます:\\n\\n`Success`\\n: コンテナの診断が成功しました。\\n\\n`Failure`\\n: コンテナの診断が失敗しました。\\n\\n`Unknown`\\n: コンテナの診断自体が失敗しました(何も実行する必要はなく、kubeletはさらにチェックを行います)。\\n\\n### Probeの種類 {#types-of-probe}\\n\\nkubeletは3種類のProbeを実行中のコンテナで行い、また反応することができます:\\n\\n`livenessProbe`\\n: コンテナが動いているかを示します。\\n  livenessProbeに失敗すると、kubeletはコンテナを殺します、そしてコンテナは[restart policy](#restart-policy)に従います。\\n  コンテナにlivenessProbeが設定されていない場合、デフォルトの状態は`Success`です。\\n\\n`readinessProbe`\\n: コンテナがリクエスト応答する準備ができているかを示します。\\n  readinessProbeに失敗すると、エンドポイントコントローラーにより、ServiceからそのPodのIPアドレスが削除されます。\\n  initial delay前のデフォルトのreadinessProbeの初期値は`Failure`です。\\n  コンテナにreadinessProbeが設定されていない場合、デフォルトの状態は`Success`です。\\n\\n`startupProbe`\\n: コンテナ内のアプリケーションが起動したかどうかを示します。\\n  startupProbeが設定された場合、完了するまでその他のすべてのProbeは無効になります。\\n  startupProbeに失敗すると、kubeletはコンテナを殺します、そしてコンテナは[restart policy](#restart-policy)に従います。\\n  コンテナにstartupProbeが設定されていない場合、デフォルトの状態は`Success`です。\\n\\nlivenessProbe、readinessProbeまたはstartupProbeを設定する方法の詳細については、[Liveness Probe、Readiness ProbeおよびStartup Probeを使用する](/ja/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes/)を参照してください。\\n\\n#### livenessProbeをいつ使うべきか? {#when-should-you-use-a-liveness-probe}\\n\\n{{< feature-state for_k8s_version=\\\"v1.0\\\" state=\\\"stable\\\" >}}\\n\\nコンテナ自体に問題が発生した場合や状態が悪くなった際にクラッシュすることができればlivenessProbeは不要です。\\nこの場合kubeletが自動でPodの`restartPolicy`に基づいたアクションを実行します。\\n\\nProbeに失敗したときにコンテナを殺したり再起動させたりするには、livenessProbeを設定し`restartPolicy`をAlwaysまたはOnFailureにします。\\n\\n#### `Unknown`: 진단 자체가 실패하였으므로 아무런 액션도 수행되면 안됨.\\n\\nkubelet은 실행 중인 컨테이너들에 대해서 선택적으로 세 가지 종류의 프로브를 수행하고\\n그에 반응할 수 있다.\\n\\n* `livenessProbe`: 컨테이너가 동작 중인지 여부를 나타낸다. 만약\\n   활성 프로브(liveness probe)에 실패한다면, `startupProbe`: 컨테이너 내의 애플리케이션이 시작되었는지를 나타낸다.\\n   스타트업 프로브(startup probe)가 주어진 경우, 성공할 때까지 다른 나머지 프로브는\\n   활성화되지 않는다. 만약 스타트업 프로브가 실패하면, kubelet이 컨테이너를 죽이고,\\n   컨테이너는 [재시작 정책](#restart-policy)에 따라 처리된다. 컨테이너에 스타트업\\n   프로브가 없는 경우, 기본 상태는 `Success`이다.\\n\\n활성, 준비성 및 스타트업 프로브를 설정하는 방법에 대한 추가적인 정보는,\\n[활성, 준비성 및 스타트업 프로브 설정하기](/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-probes/)를 참조하면 된다.\\n\\n### 언제 활성 프로브를 사용해야 하는가?\\n\\n{{< feature-state for_k8s_version=\\\"v1.0\\\" state=\\\"stable\\\" >}}\\n\\n만약 컨테이너 속 프로세스가 어떠한 이슈에 직면하거나 건강하지 못한\\n상태(unhealthy)가 되는 등 프로세스 자체의 문제로 중단될 수 있더라도, 활성 프로브가\\n반드시 필요한 것은 아니다. 그 경우에는 kubelet이 파드의 `restartPolicy`에\\n따라서 올바른 대처를 자동적으로 수행할 것이다.\\n\\n프로브가 실패한 >}}\\n\\n프로브가 성공한 경우에만 파드에 트래픽 전송을 시작하려고 한다면,\\n준비성 프로브를 지정하길 바란다. 이 경우에서는, 준비성 프로브가 활성 프로브와 유사해\\n보일 수도 있지만, 스팩에 준비성 프로브가 존재한다는 것은 파드가\\n트래픽을 받지 않는 상태에서 시작되고 프로브가 성공하기 시작한 이후에만\\n트래픽을 받는다는 뜻이다.\\n\\n만약 컨테이너가 유지 관리를 위해서 자체 중단되게 하려면,\\n준비성 프로브를 지정하길 바란다.\\n준비성 프로브는 활성 프로브와는 다르게 준비성에 특정된 엔드포인트를 확인한다.\\n\\n만약 애플리케이션이 백엔드 서비스에 엄격한 의존성이 있다면,\\n활성 프로브와 준비성 프로브 모두 활용할 수도 있다. 활성 프로브는 애플리케이션 스스로가 건강한 상태면\\n통과하지만, 준비성 프로브는 추가적으로 요구되는 각 백-엔드 서비스가 가용한지 확인한다. 이를 이용하여,\\n오류 메시지만 응답하는 파드로\\n트래픽이 가는 것을 막을 수 있다.\\n\\n만약 컨테이너가 시동 시 대량 데이터의 로딩, 구성 파일, 또는\\n마이그레이션에 대한 작업을\\n수행해야 한다면, [스타트업 프로브](#언제-스타트업-프로브를-사용해야-하는가)를 사용하면 된다. 그러나, 만약\\nfailed 애플리케이션과 시동 중에 아직 데이터를 처리하고 있는 애플리케이션을 구분하여 탐지하고\\n싶다면, 준비성 프로브를 사용하는 것이 더 적합할 것이다.\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\n파드가 삭제될 때 요청들을 흘려 보내기(drain) 위해\\n준비성 프로브가 꼭 필요한 것은 아니다. 삭제 시에, 파드는\\n프로브의 존재 여부와 무관하게 자동으로 스스로를 준비되지 않은 상태(unready)로 변경한다.\\n파드는 파드 내의 모든 컨테이너들이 중지될 때까지 준비되지 않은 상태로\\n남아 있다.\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\n### 언제 스타트업 프로브를 사용해야 하는가?\\n\\n{{< If you put the same file\\nin the search paths list below, kubelet uses it as the credential provider when pulling images.\\n\\n* `{--root-dir:-/var/lib/kubelet}/config.json`\\n* `{cwd of kubelet}/config.json`\\n* `${HOME}/.docker/config.json`\\n* `/.docker/config.json`\\n* `{--root-dir:-/var/lib/kubelet}/.dockercfg`\\n* `{cwd of kubelet}/.dockercfg`\\n* `${HOME}/.dockercfg`\\n* `/.dockercfg`\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\nYou may have to set `HOME=/root` explicitly in the environment of the kubelet process.\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\nHere are the recommended steps to configuring your nodes to use a private registry. It\\nwill not work reliably if your cloud provider manages nodes and replaces\\nthem automatically.\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\nBy default, the kubelet tries to pull each image from the specified registry.\\nHowever, if the `imagePullPolicy` property of the container is set to `IfNotPresent` or `Never`,\\nthen a local image is used (preferentially or exclusively, respectively).\\n\\nIf you >}}\\nThis is the recommended approach to run containers based on images\\nin private registries.\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\nKubernetes supports specifying container image registry keys on a Pod.\\n\\n#### However, if you\\nare using one of the built-in types, you must meet all the requirements defined\\nfor that type.\\n\\nIf you are defining a type of secret that's for public use, follow the convention\\nand structure the secret type to have your domain name before the name, separated\\nby a `/`. For example: `cloud-hosting.example.net/cloud-api-credentials`.\\n\\n### Opaque secrets\\n\\n`Opaque` is the default Secret type if omitted from a Secret configuration file.\\nWhen you create a Secret using `kubectl`, you will use the `generic`\\nsubcommand to indicate an `Opaque` Secret type. For example, the following\\ncommand creates an empty Secret of type `Opaque`.\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl create secret generic empty-secret\\nkubectl get secret empty-secret\\n```\\n\\nThe output looks like:\\n\\n```\\nNAME           TYPE     DATA   AGE\\nempty-secret   Opaque   0      2m6s\\n```\\n\\nThe `DATA` column shows the number of data items stored in the Secret.\\nIn this case, `0` means you have created an empty Secret.\\n\\n### Service account token Secrets\\n\\nA `kubernetes.io/service-account-token` type of Secret is used to store a\\ntoken credential that identifies a\\n{{< glossary_tooltip text=\\\"service account\\\" term_id=\\\"service-account\\\" >}}.\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\nVersions of Kubernetes before v1.22 automatically created credentials for\\naccessing the Kubernetes API. This older mechanism was based on creating token\\nSecrets that could then be mounted into running Pods.\\nIn more recent versions, including Kubernetes v{{< skew currentVersion >}}, API\\ncredentials are obtained directly by using the\\n[TokenRequest](/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/authentication-resources/token-request-v1/)\\nAPI, and are mounted into Pods using a\\n[projected volume](/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/service-accounts-admin/#bound-service-account-token-volume).\\nThe tokens obtained using this method have bounded lifetimes, and are\\nautomatically invalidated when the Pod they are mounted into is deleted.\\n\\nYou can still\\n[manually create](/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#manually-create-a-service-account-api-token)\\na service account token Secret; for example, if you need a token that never\\nexpires. However, using the\\n[TokenRequest](/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/authentication-resources/token-request-v1/)\\nsubresource to obtain a token to access the API is recommended instead.\\nYou can use the\\n[`kubectl create token`](/docs/reference/generated/kubectl/kubectl-commands#-em-token-em-)\\ncommand to obtain a token from the `TokenRequest` API.\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\nYou should only create a service account token Secret object\\nif you can't use the `TokenRequest` API to obtain a token,\\nand the security exposure of persisting a non-expiring token credential\\nin a readable API object is acceptable to you.\\n\\nWhen using this Secret type, you need to ensure that the\\n`kubernetes.io/service-account.name` annotation is set to an existing\\nservice account name. If you are creating both the ServiceAccount and\\nthe Secret objects, you should create the ServiceAccount object first.\\n\\nAfter the Secret is created, a Kubernetes {{< glossary_tooltip text=\\\"controller\\\" term_id=\\\"controller\\\" >}}\\nfills in some other fields such as the `kubernetes.io/service-account.uid` annotation, and the\\n`token` key in the `data` field, which is populated with an authentication token.\\n\\nThe following example configuration declares a service account token Secret:\\n\\n```yaml\\napiVersion: v1\\nkind: Secret\\nmetadata:\\n  name: secret-sa-sample\\n  annotations:\\n    kubernetes.io/service-account.name: \\\"sa-name\\\"\\ntype: kubernetes.io/service-account-token\\ndata:\\n  # You can include additional key value pairs as you do with Opaque Secrets\\n  extra: YmFyCg==\\n```\\n\\nAfter creating the Secret, wait for Kubernetes to populate the `token` key in the `data` field.\\n\\nSee the [ServiceAccount](/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/)\\ndocumentation for more information on how service accounts work.\\nYou can also check the `automountServiceAccountToken` field and the\\n`serviceAccountName` field of the\\n[`Pod`](/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/{{< param \\\"version\\\" >}}/#pod-v1-core)\\nfor information on referencing service account credentials from within Pods.\\n\\n### Docker config Secrets\\n\\nYou can use one of the following `type` values to create a Secret to\\nstore the credentials for accessing a container image registry:\\n\\n- `kubernetes.io/dockercfg`\\n- `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`\\n\\nThe `kubernetes.io/dockercfg` type is reserved to store a serialized\\n`~/.dockercfg` which is the legacy format for configuring Docker command line.\\nWhen using this Secret type, you have to ensure the Secret `data` field\\ncontains a `.dockercfg` key whose value is content of a `~/.dockercfg` file\\nencoded in the base64 format.\\n\\nThe `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` type is designed for storing a serialized\\nJSON that follows the same format rules as the `~/.docker/config.json` file\\nwhich is a new format for `~/.dockercfg`.\\nWhen using this Secret type, the `data` field of the Secret object must\\ncontain a `.dockerconfigjson` key, in which the content for the\\n`~/.docker/config.json` file is provided as a base64 encoded string.\\n\\nBelow is an example for a `kubernetes.io/dockercfg` type of Secret:\\n\\n```yaml\\napiVersion: v1\\nkind: Secret\\nmetadata:\\n  name: secret-dockercfg\\ntype: kubernetes.io/dockercfg\\ndata:\\n  .dockercfg: |\\n    \\\"<base64 encoded ~/.dockercfg file>\\\"\\n```\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\nIf you do not want to perform the base64 encoding, you can choose to use the\\n`stringData` field instead.\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\nWhen you create these types of Secrets using a manifest, the API\\nserver checks whether the expected key exists in the `data` field, and\\nit verifies if the value provided can be parsed as a valid JSON. The API\\nserver doesn't validate if the JSON actually is a Docker config file.\\n\\nWhen you do not have a Docker config file, or you want to use `kubectl`\\nto create a Secret for accessing a container registry, you can do:\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl create secret docker-registry secret-tiger-docker \\\\\\n  --docker-email=tiger@acme.example \\\\\\n  --docker-username=tiger \\\\\\n  --docker-password=pass1234 \\\\\\n  --docker-server=my-registry.example:5000\\n```\\n\\nThat command creates a Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`.\\nIf you dump the `.data.dockerconfigjson` field from that new Secret and then\\ndecode it from base64:\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl get secret secret-tiger-docker -o jsonpath='{.data.*}' | base64 -d\\n```\\n\\nthen the output is equivalent to this JSON document (which is also a valid\\nDocker configuration file):\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"auths\\\": {\\n    \\\"my-registry.example:5000\\\": {\\n      \\\"username\\\": \\\"tiger\\\",\\n      \\\"password\\\": \\\"pass1234\\\",\\n      \\\"email\\\": \\\"tiger@acme.example\\\",\\n      \\\"auth\\\": \\\"dGlnZXI6cGFzczEyMzQ=\\\"\\n    }\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\nThe `auth` value there is base64 encoded; it is obscured but not secret.\\nAnyone who can read that Secret can learn the registry access bearer token.\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\n### Basic authentication Secret\\n\\nThe `kubernetes.io/basic-auth` type is provided for storing credentials needed\\nfor basic authentication. When using this Secret type, the `data` field of the\\nSecret must contain one of the following two keys:\\n\\n- `username`: the user name for authentication\\n- `password`: the password or token for authentication\\n\\nBoth values for the above two keys are base64 encoded strings. You can, of\\ncourse, provide the clear text content using the `stringData` for Secret\\ncreation.\\n\\nThe following manifest is an example of a basic authentication Secret:\\n\\n```yaml\\napiVersion: v1\\nkind: Secret\\nmetadata:\\n  name: secret-basic-auth\\ntype: kubernetes.io/basic-auth\\nstringData:\\n  username: admin      # required field for kubernetes.io/basic-auth\\n  password: t0p-Secret # required field for kubernetes.io/basic-auth\\n```\\n\\nThe basic authentication Secret type is provided only for convenience.\\nYou can create an `Opaque` type for credentials used for basic authentication.\\nHowever, using the defined and public Secret type (`kubernetes.io/basic-auth`) helps other\\npeople to understand the purpose of your Secret, and sets a convention for what key names\\nto expect.\\nThe Kubernetes API verifies that the required keys are set for a Secret of this type.\\n\\n### SSH authentication secrets\\n\\nThe builtin type `kubernetes.io/ssh-auth` is provided for storing data used in\\nSSH authentication. When using this Secret type, you will have to specify a\\n`ssh-privatekey` key-value pair in the `data` (or `stringData`) field\\nas the SSH credential to use.\\n\\nThe following manifest is an example of a Secret used for SSH public/private\\nkey authentication:\\n\\n```yaml\\napiVersion: v1\\nkind: Secret\\nmetadata:\\n  name: secret-ssh-auth\\ntype: kubernetes.io/ssh-auth\\ndata:\\n  # the data is abbreviated in this example\\n  ssh-privatekey: |\\n     MIIEpQIBAAKCAQEAulqb/Y ...\\n```\\n\\nThe SSH authentication Secret type is provided only for user's convenience.\\nYou could instead create an `Opaque` type Secret for credentials used for SSH authentication.\\nHowever, using the defined and public Secret type (`kubernetes.io/ssh-auth`) helps other\\npeople to understand the purpose of your Secret, and sets a convention for what key names\\nto expect.\\nand the API server does verify if the required keys are provided in a Secret configuration.\\n\\n{{< caution >}}\\nSSH private keys do not establish trusted communication between an SSH client and\\nhost server on their own. A secondary means of establishing trust is needed to\\nmitigate \\\"man in the middle\\\" attacks, such as a `known_hosts` file added to a ConfigMap.\\n{{< /caution >}}\\n\\n### TLS secrets\\n\\nKubernetes provides a builtin Secret type `kubernetes.io/tls` for storing\\na certificate and its associated key that are typically used for TLS.\\n\\nOne common use for TLS secrets is to configure encryption in transit for\\nan [Ingress](/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/), but you can also use it\\nwith other resources or directly in your workload.\\nWhen using this type of Secret, the `tls.key` and the `tls.crt` key must be provided\\nin the `data` (or `stringData`) field of the Secret configuration, although the API\\nserver doesn't actually validate the values for each key.\\n\\nThe following YAML contains an example config for a TLS Secret:\\n\\n```yaml\\napiVersion: v1\\nkind: Secret\\nmetadata:\\n  name: secret-tls\\ntype: kubernetes.io/tls\\ndata:\\n  # the data is abbreviated in this example\\n  tls.crt: |\\n    MIIC2DCCAcCgAwIBAgIBATANBgkqh ...\\n  tls.key: |\\n    MIIEpgIBAAKCAQEA7yn3bRHQ5FHMQ ...\\n```\\n\\nThe TLS Secret type is provided for user's convenience. You can create an `Opaque`\\nfor credentials used for TLS server and/or client. However, using the builtin Secret\\ntype helps ensure the consistency of Secret format in your project; the API server\\ndoes verify if the required keys are provided in a Secret configuration.\\n\\nWhen creating a TLS Secret using `kubectl`, you can use the `tls` subcommand\\nas shown in the following example:\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl create secret tls my-tls-secret \\\\\\n  --cert=path/to/cert/file \\\\\\n  --key=path/to/key/file\\n```\\n\\nThe public/private key pair must exist before hand. The public key certificate\\nfor `--cert` must be DER format as per\\n[Section 5.1 of RFC 7468](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7468#section-5.1),\\nand must match the given private key for `--key` (PKCS #8 in DER format;\\n[Section 11 of RFC 7468](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7468#section-11)).\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\nA kubernetes.io/tls Secret stores the Base64-encoded DER data for keys and\\ncertificates. `type` field of\\nthe [Secret](/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/config-and-storage-resources/secret-v1/)\\nresource, or certain equivalent `kubectl` command line flags (if available).\\nThe Secret type performed and the constraints\\nKubernetes imposes on them.\\n\\n| Built-in Type | Usage |\\n|--------------|-------|\\n| `Opaque`     |  arbitrary user-defined data |\\n| data for a TLS client or server |\\n| `bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token` | bootstrap token data |\\n\\nYou can define and use your own Secret type by assigning a non-empty string as the\\n`type` value However, if you\\nare using one of the built-in types, you must meet all the requirements defined\\nfor that type.\\n\\nIf you are defining a type of secret that's for public use, follow the convention\\nand structure the secret type to have your domain name before the name, separated\\nby a `/`. For example, the following\\ncommand creates an empty Secret of type `Opaque`.\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl create secret generic empty-secret\\nkubectl get secret empty-secret\\n```\\n\\nThe output looks like:\\n\\n```\\nNAME           TYPE     DATA   AGE\\nempty-secret   Opaque   0      2m6s\\n```\\n\\nThe `DATA` column shows the number of data items stored in the Secret.\\nIn this case, `0` means you have created an empty Secret.\\n\\n### Service account token Secrets\\n\\nA `kubernetes.io/service-account-token` type of Secret is used to store a\\ntoken credential that identifies a\\n{{< glossary_tooltip text=\\\"service account\\\" term_id=\\\"service-account\\\" >}}.\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\nVersions of Kubernetes before v1.22 automatically created credentials for\\naccessing the Kubernetes API. Required.\\n- `token-secret`: A random 16 character string as the actual token secret. Required.\\n- `description`: A human-readable string that describes what the token is\\n  used for. Optional.\\n- `expiration`: An absolute UTC time using [RFC3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339) specifying when the token\\n  should be expired. The Secret `data` field must contain a\\n  `.dockerconfigjson` key for which the value is the content of a base64\\n  encoded `~/.docker/config.json` file.\\n-->\\n- `kubernetes.io/dockercfg`：存放 `~/.dockercfg` 文件的序列化形式，它是配置 Docker\\n  命令行的一种老旧形式。Secret 的 `data` 字段包含名为 `.dockercfg` 的主键，\\n  其值是用 base64 编码的某 `~/.dockercfg` 文件的内容。\\n- `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`：存放 JSON 数据的序列化形式，\\n  该 JSON 也遵从 `~/.docker/config.json` 文件的格式规则，而后者是 `~/.dockercfg`\\n  的新版本格式。使用此 Secret 类型时，Secret 对象的 `data` 字段必须包含\\n  `.dockerconfigjson` 键，其键值为 base64 编码的字符串包含 `~/.docker/config.json`\\n  文件的内容。\\n\\n<!--\\nBelow is an example for a `kubernetes.io/dockercfg` type of Secret:\\n-->\\n下面是一个 `kubernetes.io/dockercfg` 类型 Secret 的示例：\\n\\n{{% code_sample language=\\\"yaml\\\" file=\\\"secret/dockercfg-secret.yaml\\\" %}}\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\n<!--\\nIf you do not want to perform the base64 encoding, you can choose to use the\\n`stringData` field instead.\\n-->\\n如果你不希望执行 base64 编码转换，可以使用 `stringData` 字段代替。\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\n<!--\\nWhen you create Docker config Secrets using a manifest, the API\\nserver checks whether the expected key exists in the `data` field, and\\nit verifies if the value provided can be parsed as a valid JSON. The API\\nserver doesn't validate if the JSON actually is a Docker config file.\\n\\nYou can also use `kubectl` to create a Secret for accessing a container\\nregistry, such as when you don't have a Docker configuration file:\\n-->\\n当你使用清单文件通过 Docker 配置来创建 Secret 时，API 服务器会检查 `data` 字段中是否存在所期望的主键，\\n并且验证其中所提供的键值是否是合法的 JSON 数据。\\n不过，API 服务器不会检查 JSON 数据本身是否是一个合法的 Docker 配置文件内容。\\n\\n你还可以使用 `kubectl` 创建一个 Secret 来访问容器仓库时，\\n当你没有 Docker 配置文件时你可以这样做：\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl create secret docker-registry secret-tiger-docker \\\\\\n  --docker-email=tiger@acme.example \\\\\\n  --docker-username=tiger \\\\\\n  --docker-password=pass1234 \\\\\\n  --docker-server=my-registry.example:5000\\n```\\n\\n<!--\\nThis command creates a Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`.\\n\\nRetrieve the `.data.dockerconfigjson` field from that new Secret and decode the\\ndata:\\n-->\\n此命令创建一个类型为 `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` 的 Secret。\\n\\n从这个新的 Secret 中获取 `.data.dockerconfigjson` 字段并执行数据解码：\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl get secret secret-tiger-docker -o jsonpath='{.data.*}' | base64 -d\\n```\\n\\n<!--\\nThe output is equivalent to the following JSON document (which is also a valid\\nDocker configuration file):\\n-->\\n输出等价于以下 JSON 文档（这也是一个有效的 Docker 配置文件）：\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"auths\\\": {\\n    \\\"my-registry.example:5000\\\": {\\n      \\\"username\\\": \\\"tiger\\\",\\n      \\\"password\\\": \\\"pass1234\\\",\\n      \\\"email\\\": \\\"tiger@acme.example\\\",\\n      \\\"auth\\\": \\\"dGlnZXI6cGFzczEyMzQ=\\\"\\n    }\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n{{< caution >}}\\n<!--\\nThe `auth` value there is base64 encoded; Since\\nclosures attempt to infer the types of their parameters, they also infer how\\nthose parameters are borrowed. Closures make that inference by looking at how\\nthey are used. Consider the example in Listing 13-5 that has functions that\\nborrow immutably, borrow mutably, and move their parameters, then closures that\\nreference values from their environment and call each of the functions. We'll\\nsee how this affects inference of when a value is borrowed:\\n\\n<figure>\\n<span class=\\\"filename\\\">Filename: src/main.rs</span>\\n\\n```rust\\n#[derive(Debug)]\\nstruct Foo;\\n\\nfn borrows(f: &Foo) {\\n    println!(\\\"Took {:?} by reference.\\\", f);\\n}\\n\\nfn borrows_mut(f: &mut Foo) {\\n    println!(\\\"Took {:?} by mutable reference.\\\", f);\\n}\\n\\nfn moves(f: Foo) {\\n    println!(\\\"Took ownership of {:?}.\\\", f);\\n}\\n\\nfn main() {\\n    let f1 = Foo;\\n    let closure_that_borrows = |x| borrows(x);\\n    closure_that_borrows(&f1);\\n\\n    let mut f2 = Foo;\\n    let closure_that_borrows_mut = |y| borrows_mut(y);\\n    closure_that_borrows_mut(&mut f2);\\n\\n    let f3 = Foo;\\n    let closure_that_moves = |z| moves(z);\\n    closure_that_moves(f3);\\n}\\n```\\n\\n<figcaption>\\n\\nListing 13-5: Closures that borrow, borrow mutably, and take ownership of their\\nparameters, which is inferred from how the closure body uses the parameters\\n\\n</figcaption>\\n</figure>\\n\\nHere, Rust is able to look at how we use the parameters of each closure inside\\ntheir bodies. kubelet은 활성화된 각 서비스에 대한 환경 변수\\n집합을 추가한다. `{SVCNAME}_SERVICE_HOST`와 `{SVCNAME}_SERVICE_PORT` 변수를\\n추가하는데, 이때 서비스 이름은 대문자로 바뀌고 하이픈은 언더스코어로 변환된다.\\n\\n\\n예를 들어, TCP 포트 6379를 노출하고 클러스터 IP 주소 10.0.0.11이 할당된\\n서비스 `redis-primary`는 다음과 같은 \\n환경 변수를 생성한다.\\n\\n```shell\\nREDIS_PRIMARY_SERVICE_HOST=10.0.0.11\\nREDIS_PRIMARY_SERVICE_PORT=6379\\nREDIS_PRIMARY_PORT=tcp://10.0.0.11:6379\\nREDIS_PRIMARY_PORT_6379_TCP=tcp://10.0.0.11:6379\\nREDIS_PRIMARY_PORT_6379_TCP_PROTO=tcp\\nREDIS_PRIMARY_PORT_6379_TCP_PORT=6379\\nREDIS_PRIMARY_PORT_6379_TCP_ADDR=10.0.0.11\\n```\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\n서비스에 접근해야 하는 파드가 있고, 환경 변수 방식을 사용하여 포트와\\n클러스터 IP를 클라이언트 파드에 노출하는 경우, 클라이언트 파드가 존재하기\\n*전에* 서비스를 생성해야 한다. 그렇지 않으면 해당 클라이언트 파드는 환경\\n변수가 채워지지 않는다.\\n\\n서비스의 클러스터 IP를 찾는 데 DNS만 사용한다면, 이러한 순서 문제를\\n걱정할 필요가 없다.\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\n쿠버네티스는 또한 도커 엔진의 \\\"_[레거시 컨테이너 링크](https://docs.docker.com/network/links/)_\\\"\\n기능과 호환되는 변수도 지원하고 제공한다.\\n쿠버네티스에서 이것이 어떻게 구현되어 있는지 확인하려면\\n[`makeLinkVariables`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dd2d12f6dc0e654c15d5db57a5f9f6ba61192726/pkg/kubelet/envvars/envvars.go#L72)를 참고한다.\\n\\n### DNS\\n\\n[애드온](/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/addons/)을 사용하여 쿠버네티스\\n클러스터에 DNS 서비스를 설정할 수 있다(거의 항상 그렇게 해야 한다).\\n\\nCoreDNS와 같은 클러스터를 인식하는 DNS 서버는 새로운 서비스가 있는지\\n쿠버네티스 API를 감시하고, 각각에 대해 DNS 레코드 집합을 생성한다. 클러스터\\n전체에서 DNS가 활성화되어 있다면, 모든 파드는 자동으로 서비스를 해당 DNS\\n이름으로 확인할 수 있어야 한다.\\n\\n예를 들어, 쿠버네티스 네임스페이스 `my-ns`에 `my-service`라는 서비스가\\n있다면, 컨트롤 플레인과 DNS 서비스가 함께 작동하여 `my-service.my-ns`에\\n대한 DNS 레코드를 생성한다. `my-ns` 네임스페이스의 파드는 `my-service`에\\n대한 이름 조회를 수행하여 해당 서비스를 찾을 수 있어야 한다\\n(`my-service.my-ns`도 마찬가지로 동작한다).\\n\\n다른 네임스페이스의 파드는 이름을 `my-service.my-ns`로 한정해야 한다.\\n이러한 이름은 서비스에 할당된 클러스터 IP로 확인된다.\\n\\n쿠버네티스는 또한 이름이 지정된 포트에 대해 DNS SRV(서비스) 레코드도\\n지원한다. `my-service.my-ns` 서비스에 프로토콜이 `TCP`로 설정된 `http`라는\\n이름의 포트가 있다면, `_http._tcp.my-service.my-ns`에 대한 DNS SRV 쿼리를\\n수행하여 IP 주소는 물론 `http`의 포트 번호도 발견할 수 있다.\\n\\n쿠버네티스 DNS 서버는 `ExternalName` 서비스에 접근할 수 있는 유일한 방법이다.\\n`ExternalName` 확인에 대한 자세한 내용은\\n[서비스 및 파드용 DNS](/docs/concepts/services-networking/dns-pod-service/)에서 찾을 수 있다.\\n\\n<!-- name: secret-volume\\n      secret:\\n        secretName: test-db-secret\\n    containers:\\n    - name: db-client-container\\n      image: myClientImage\\n      volumeMounts:\\n      - name: secret-volume\\n        readOnly: true\\n        mountPath: \\\"/etc/secret-volume\\\"\\nEOF\\n```\\n\\n동일한 `kustomization.yaml`에 파드를 추가한다.\\n\\n```shell\\ncat <<EOF >> kustomization.yaml\\nresources:\\n- pod.yaml\\nEOF\\n```\\n\\n다음을 실행하여 API 서버에 이러한 모든 오브젝트를 적용한다.\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl apply -k .\\n```\\n\\n두 컨테이너 모두 각 컨테이너의 환경에 대한 값을 가진 파일시스템에 \\n다음의 파일이 존재한다.\\n\\n```\\n/etc/secret-volume/username\\n/etc/secret-volume/password\\n```\\n\\n두 파드의 사양이 한 필드에서만 어떻게 다른지 확인한다. 이를 통해\\n공통 파드 템플릿에서 다양한 기능을 가진 파드를 생성할 수 있다.\\n\\n두 개의 서비스 어카운트를 사용하여 기본 파드 명세를 더욱 단순화할 수 있다.\\n\\n1. `prod-db-secret` 을 가진 `prod-user`\\n1. `test-db-secret` 을 가진 `test-user`\\n\\n파드 명세는 다음과 같이 단축된다.\\n\\n```yaml\\napiVersion: v1\\nkind: Pod\\nmetadata:\\n  name: prod-db-client-pod\\n  labels:\\n    name: prod-db-client\\nspec:\\n  serviceAccount: prod-db-client\\n  containers:\\n  - 오브젝트. 각 노드는 연관된 리스 오브젝트를 갖는다.\\n\\n노드의 `.status`에 비하면, 리스는 경량의 리소스이다.\\n큰 규모의 클러스터에서는 리스를 하트비트에 사용하여 \\n업데이트로 인한 성능 영향을 줄일 수 있다.\\n\\nkubelet은 노드의 `.status` 생성과 업데이트 및\\n관련된 리스의 업데이트를 담당한다. \\n\\n- 생성하고 업데이트한다. 리스 업데이트는 노드의 `.status` 업데이트와는 독립적이다.\\n  만약 리스 업데이트가 실패하면, kubelet은 200밀리초에서 시작하고\\n  7초의 상한을 갖는 지수적 백오프를 사용해서 재시도한다.\\n\\n### 노드 컨트롤러\\n\\n노드 {{< glossary_tooltip text=\\\"컨트롤러\\\" term_id=\\\"controller\\\" >}}는\\n노드의 다양한 측면을 관리하는 쿠버네티스 컨트롤 플레인 컴포넌트이다.\\n\\n노드 컨트롤러는 노드가 생성되어 유지되는 동안 다양한 역할을 한다. 첫째는 등록 시점에\\n(CIDR 할당이 사용토록 설정된 경우) 노드에 CIDR 블럭을 할당하는 것이다.\\n\\n두 번째는 노드 컨트롤러의 내부 노드 리스트를 클라우드 제공사업자의\\n사용 가능한 머신 리스트 정보를 근거로 최신상태로 유지하는 것이다. 클라우드 환경에서\\n동작 중일 경우, 노드상태가 불량할 때마다, 노드 컨트롤러는\\n해당 노드용 VM이 여전히 사용 가능한지에 대해 클라우드 제공사업자에게 묻는다. 사용 가능하지 않을 경우,\\n노드 컨트롤러는 노드 리스트로부터 그 노드를 설정한다.\\n- 노드가 계속 접근 불가능 상태로 남아있는 경우, 해당 노드의 모든 파드에 대해서\\n  [API를 이용한 축출](/ko/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/api-eviction/)을\\n  트리거한다. 기본적으로, 노드 컨트롤러는 노드를\\n  `Unknown`으로 마킹한 뒤 5분을 기다렸다가\\n  최초의 축출 `--node-eviction-rate`(기본값 0.1)로\\n축출 속도를 제한한다. 이 말은 10초당 1개의 노드를 초과하여\\n파드 축출을 하지 않는다는 의미가 된다.\\n\\n노드 축출 행위는 주어진 가용성 영역 내 하나의 노드가 상태가 불량할\\n경우 변화한다. 노드 컨트롤러는 영역 내 동시에 상태가 불량한 노드의 퍼센티지가 얼마나 이하면 - 기본값 50) 축출이 중지된다.\\n- 이외의 경우, 축출 속도는 초당\\n  `--secondary-node-eviction-rate`(기본값 0.01)로 감소된다.\\n\\n이 정책들이 가용성 영역 단위로 실행되어지는 이유는 나머지가 연결되어 있는 동안\\n하나의 가용성 영역이 컨트롤 플레인으로부터 분할되어 질 수도 있기 때문이다.\\n만약 클러스터가 여러 클라우드 제공사업자의 가용성 영역에 걸쳐 있지 않는 이상,\\n축출 매커니즘은 영역 별 가용성을 고려하지 않는다.\\n\\n노드가 가용성 영역들에 걸쳐 퍼져 있는 주된 이유는 하나의 전체 영역이\\n장애가 발생할 경우 워크로드가 상태 양호한 영역으로 이전되어질 수 있도록 하기 위해서이다.\\n그러므로, 하나의 영역 내 모든 노드들이 상태가 불량하면 노드 컨트롤러는\\n`--node-eviction-rate` 의 정상 속도로 축출한다. 코너 케이스란 모든 영역이\\n완전히 상태불량(클러스터 내 양호한 노드가 없는 경우)한 경우이다.\\n이러한 경우, 노드 컨트롤러는 컨트롤 플레인과 노드 간 연결에 문제가\\n있는 것으로 간주하고 축출을 실행하지 않는다. For example: `cloud-hosting.example.net/cloud-api-credentials`.\\n-->\\n如果你要定义一种公开使用的 Secret 类型，请遵守 Secret 类型的约定和结构，\\n在类型名签名添加域名，并用 `/` 隔开。\\n例如：`cloud-hosting.example.net/cloud-api-credentials`。\\n\\n<!--\\n### Opaque secrets\\n\\n`Opaque` is the default Secret type if omitted from a Secret configuration file.\\nWhen you create a Secret using `kubectl`, you will use the `generic`\\nsubcommand to indicate an `Opaque` Secret type. For example, the following\\ncommand creates an empty Secret of type `Opaque`.\\n-->\\n### Opaque Secret\\n\\n当 Secret 配置文件中未作显式设定时，默认的 Secret 类型是 `Opaque`。\\n当你使用 `kubectl` 来创建一个 Secret 时，你会使用 `generic`\\n子命令来标明要创建的是一个 `Opaque` 类型 Secret。\\n例如，下面的命令会创建一个空的 `Opaque` 类型 Secret 对象：\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl create secret generic empty-secret\\nkubectl get secret empty-secret\\n```\\n\\n<!--\\nThe output looks like:\\n-->\\n输出类似于\\n\\n```\\nNAME           TYPE     DATA   AGE\\nempty-secret   Opaque   0      2m6s\\n```\\n\\n<!--\\nThe `DATA` column shows the number of data items stored in the Secret.\\nIn this case, `0` means you have created an empty Secret.\\n-->\\n`DATA` 列显示 Secret 中保存的数据条目个数。\\n在这个例子中，`0` 意味着你刚刚创建了一个空的 Secret。\\n\\n<!--\\n### Service account token Secrets\\n\\nA `kubernetes.io/service-account-token` type of Secret is used to store a\\ntoken credential that identifies a\\n{{< glossary_tooltip text=\\\"service account\\\" term_id=\\\"service-account\\\" >}}.\\n-->\\n### 服务账号令牌 Secret  {#service-account-token-secrets}\\n\\n类型为 `kubernetes.io/service-account-token` 的 Secret\\n用来存放标识某{{< glossary_tooltip text=\\\"服务账号\\\" term_id=\\\"service-account\\\" >}}的令牌凭据。\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\n<!--\\nVersions of Kubernetes before v1.22 automatically created credentials for\\naccessing the Kubernetes API. This older mechanism was based on creating token\\nSecrets that could then be mounted into running Pods.\\nIn more recent versions, including Kubernetes v{{< skew currentVersion >}}, API\\ncredentials are obtained directly by using the\\n[TokenRequest](/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/authentication-resources/token-request-v1/)\\nAPI, and are mounted into Pods using a\\n[projected volume](/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/service-accounts-admin/#bound-service-account-token-volume).\\nThe tokens obtained using this method have bounded lifetimes, and are\\nautomatically invalidated when the Pod they are mounted into is deleted.\\n-->\\nKubernetes 在 v1.22 版本之前都会自动创建用来访问 Kubernetes API 的凭据。\\n这一老的机制是基于创建可被挂载到运行中 Pod 内的令牌 Secret 来实现的。\\n在最近的版本中，包括 Kubernetes v{{< skew currentVersion >}} 中，API 凭据是直接通过\\n[TokenRequest](/zh-cn/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/authentication-resources/token-request-v1/)\\nAPI 来获得的，这一凭据会使用[投射卷](/zh-cn/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/service-accounts-admin/#bound-service-account-token-volume)挂载到\\nPod 中。使用这种方式获得的令牌有确定的生命期，并且在挂载它们的 Pod 被删除时自动作废。\\n\\n<!--\\nYou can still\\n[manually create](/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#manually-create-a-service-account-api-token)\\na service account token Secret; for example, if you need a token that never\\nexpires. However, using the\\n[TokenRequest](/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/authentication-resources/token-request-v1/)\\nsubresource to obtain a token to access the API is recommended instead.\\nYou can use the\\n[`kubectl create token`](/docs/reference/generated/kubectl/kubectl-commands#-em-token-em-)\\ncommand to obtain a token from the `TokenRequest` API.\\n-->\\n你仍然可以[手动创建](/zh-cn/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#manually-create-a-service-account-api-token)\\n服务账号令牌。例如，当你需要一个永远都不过期的令牌时。\\n不过，仍然建议使用 [TokenRequest](/zh-cn/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/authentication-resources/token-request-v1/)\\n子资源来获得访问 API 服务器的令牌。\\n你可以使用 [`kubectl create token`](/docs/reference/generated/kubectl/kubectl-commands#-em-token-em-)\\n命令调用 `TokenRequest` API 获得令牌。\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\n<!--\\nYou should only create a service account token Secret object\\nif you can't use the `TokenRequest` API to obtain a token,\\nand the security exposure of persisting a non-expiring token credential\\nin a readable API object is acceptable to you.\\n-->\\n只有在你无法使用 `TokenRequest` API 来获取令牌，\\n并且你能够接受因为将永不过期的令牌凭据写入到可读取的 API 对象而带来的安全风险时，\\n才应该创建服务账号令牌 Secret 对象。\\n\\n<!--\\nWhen using this Secret type, you need to ensure that the\\n`kubernetes.io/service-account.name` annotation is set to an existing\\nservice account name. it is obscured but not secret.\\nAnyone who can read that Secret can learn the registry access bearer token.\\n\\nIt is suggested to use [credential providers](/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-credential-provider/) to dynamically and securely provide pull secrets on-demand.\\n-->\\n`auths` 值是 base64 编码的，其内容被屏蔽但未被加密。\\n任何能够读取该 Secret 的人都可以了解镜像库的访问令牌。\\n\\n建议使用[凭据提供程序](/zh-cn/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-credential-provider/)来动态、\\n安全地按需提供拉取 Secret。\\n{{< /caution >}}\\n\\n<!--\\n### Basic authentication Secret\\n\\nThe `kubernetes.io/basic-auth` type is provided for storing credentials needed\\nfor basic authentication. When using this Secret type, the `data` field of the\\nSecret must contain one of the following two keys:\\n\\n- `username`: the user name for authentication\\n- `password`: the password or token for authentication\\n-->\\n### 基本身份认证 Secret  {#basic-authentication-secret}\\n\\n`kubernetes.io/basic-auth` 类型用来存放用于基本身份认证所需的凭据信息。\\n使用这种 Secret 类型时，Secret 的 `data` 字段必须包含以下两个键之一：\\n\\n- `username`: 用于身份认证的用户名；\\n- `password`: 用于身份认证的密码或令牌。\\n\\n<!--\\nBoth values for the above two keys are base64 encoded strings. Subprojects have leads that function as the primary\\norganizer, domain experts, or points of contact.\\n\\n### Goals\\n\\n- Assist the projects, TOC, and other TAGs\\n- Remove ambiguity and provide guidance, increasing knowledge and understanding\\n  on the subproject domain\\n- Support projects and end users in addressing items in scope of the subproject\\n- Coordinate awareness, understanding, concurrence of the subproject\\n  deliverables with projects, end users, and other defined stakeholders\\n- Advance and accelerate the cloud native mission within the scope of the\\n  subproject\\n- Enact the technical vision of the TOC within scope of the subproject\\n\\n\\n### Formation\\n\\nSubprojects require a charter describing their purpose, scope, roles, and any\\nregular deliverables (e.g. [Subproject Initiatives]) or services they provide.\\nThis charter MUST be approved by the TOC.\\n\\nIt is strongly recommended to share a draft charter and work with the TOC early\\nto ensure a streamlined approval process.\\n\\n\\n### Requirements\\n\\n- MUST be documented including purpose, scope, roles and any deliverables or\\n  services they provide.\\n- MUST remain actively in use. A subproject that has gone 6+ months without\\n  delivering on its goal or providing a service should be considered for\\n  retirement or put on “pause”.\\n- MUST regularly report on status to leads. In the absence of defined subproject\\n  leads, responsibility for the subproject automatically falls to the Chairs and\\n  Tech Leads of the TAG. For TOC Subprojects, subproject leads fall to the TOC\\n  Shadows first and TOC Members next, as needed.\\n\\n\\n### Roles, Terms, and Elections\\n\\n#### Subproject Leads\\n\\nSubproject leads are community members and subject matter experts tasked with\\norganizing and shepherding the execution of the subproject. MAY make decisions to resolve conflicts.\\n\\n\\n##### Activity Expectations\\n\\n- Subproject Leads serve 1 year terms, and  MAY submit for re-election.\\n- Subproject Leads MAY decide to step down 지정된 명령어를 실행한다.\\n  명령어가 상태 코드 0으로 종료되면 진단이 성공한 것으로 간주한다.\\n\\n* [TCPSocketAction](/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/{{< param \\\"version\\\" >}}/#tcpsocketaction-v1-core)은\\n  지정된 포트에서 컨테이너의 IP주소에 대해 TCP 검사를 수행한다.\\n  포트가 활성화되어 있다면 진단이 성공한 것으로 간주한다.\\n\\n* [HTTPGetAction](/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/{{< param \\\"version\\\" >}}/#httpgetaction-v1-core)은\\n  지정한 포트 및 경로에서 컨테이너의 IP주소에\\n  대한 HTTP `GET` 요청을 수행한다. 응답의 상태 코드가 200 이상 400 미만이면\\n  진단이 성공한 것으로 간주한다.\\n\\n각 probe는 다음 세 가지 결과 중 하나를 가진다.\\n\\n* `Success`: 컨테이너가 진단을 통과함.\\n* `Failure`: 컨테이너가 진단에 실패함.\\n* `Unknown`: 진단 자체가 실패하였으므로 아무런 액션도 수행되면 안됨.\\n\\nkubelet은 실행 중인 컨테이너들에 대해서 선택적으로 세 가지 종류의 프로브를 수행하고\\n그에 반응할 수 있다.\\n\\n* `livenessProbe`: 컨테이너가 동작 중인지 여부를 나타낸다. 만약\\n   활성 프로브(liveness probe)에 실패한다면, kubelet은 컨테이너를 죽이고, 해당 컨테이너는\\n   [재시작 정책](#restart-policy)의 대상이 된다. 만약 컨테이너가\\n   활성 프로브를 제공하지 않는 경우, 기본 상태는 `Success`이다.\\n\\n* `readinessProbe`: 컨테이너가 요청을 처리할 준비가 되었는지 여부를 나타낸다.\\n   만약 준비성 프로브(readiness probe)가 실패한다면, 엔드포인트 컨트롤러는\\n   파드에 연관된 모든 서비스들의 엔드포인트에서 파드의 IP주소를 제거한다. 준비성 프로브의\\n   초기 지연 이전의 기본 상태는 `Failure`이다. 만약 컨테이너가 준비성 프로브를\\n   지원하지 않는다면, 기본 상태는 `Success`이다.\\n\\n* `startupProbe`: 컨테이너 내의 애플리케이션이 시작되었는지를 나타낸다.\\n   스타트업 프로브(startup probe)가 주어진 경우, 성공할 때까지 다른 나머지 프로브는\\n   활성화되지 않는다. 만약 스타트업 프로브가 실패하면, kubelet이 컨테이너를 죽이고,\\n   컨테이너는 [재시작 정책](#restart-policy)에 따라 처리된다. 컨테이너에 스타트업\\n   프로브가 없는 경우, 기본 상태는 `Success`이다.\\n\\n활성, 준비성 및 스타트업 프로브를 설정하는 방법에 대한 추가적인 정보는,\\n[활성, 준비성 및 스타트업 프로브 설정하기](/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-probes/)를 참조하면 된다.\\n\\n### 언제 활성 프로브를 사용해야 하는가?\\n\\n{{< feature-state for_k8s_version=\\\"v1.0\\\" state=\\\"stable\\\" >}}\\n\\n만약 컨테이너 속 프로세스가 어떠한 이슈에 직면하거나 건강하지 못한\\n상태(unhealthy)가 되는 등 프로세스 자체의 문제로 중단될 수 있더라도, 활성 프로브가\\n반드시 필요한 것은 아니다. 그 경우에는 kubelet이 파드의 `restartPolicy`에\\n따라서 올바른 대처를 자동적으로 수행할 것이다.\\n\\n프로브가 실패한 후 컨테이너가 종료되거나 재시작되길 원한다면, 활성 프로브를\\n지정하고, `restartPolicy`를 항상(Always) 또는 실패 시(OnFailure)로 지정한다.\\n\\n### 언제 준비성 프로브를 사용해야 하는가?\\n\\n{{< feature-state for_k8s_version=\\\"v1.0\\\" state=\\\"stable\\\" >}}\\n\\n프로브가 성공한 경우에만 파드에 트래픽 전송을 시작하려고 한다면,\\n준비성 프로브를 지정하길 바란다. 이 경우에서는, 준비성 프로브가 활성 프로브와 유사해\\n보일 수도 있지만, 스팩에 준비성 프로브가 존재한다는 것은 파드가\\n트래픽을 받지 않는 상태에서 시작되고 프로브가 성공하기 시작한 이후에만\\n트래픽을 받는다는 뜻이다.\\n만약 컨테이너가 대량의 데이터, 설정 파일들,\\n또는 시동 중 마그레이션을 처리해야 한다면, 준비성 프로브를 지정하길 바란다.\\n\\n만약 당신의 컨테이너가 유지 관리를 위해서 자체 중단되게 하려면,\\n준비성 프로브를 지정하길 바란다.\\n준비성 프로브는 활성 프로브와는 다르게 준비성에 특정된 엔드포인트를 확인한다.\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\n파드가 삭제될 때 요청들을 흘려 보내기(drain) 위해\\n준비성 프로브가 꼭 필요한 것은 아니다. 삭제 시에, 파드는\\n프로브의 존재 여부와 무관하게 자동으로 스스로를 준비되지 않은 상태(unready)로 변경한다.\\n파드는 파드 내의 모든 컨테이너들이 중지될 때까지 준비되지 않은 상태로\\n남아 있다.\\n{{< /note >}}\\n\\n### 언제 스타트업 프로브를 사용해야 하는가?\\n\\n{{< feature-state for_k8s_version=\\\"v1.20\\\" state=\\\"stable\\\" >}}\\n\\n스타트업 프로브는 서비스를 시작하는 데 오랜 시간이 걸리는 컨테이너가 있는\\n파드에 유용하다. 긴 활성 간격을 설정하는 대신, 컨테이너가 시작될 However, if you\\nare using one of the built-in types, you must meet all the requirements defined\\nfor that type.\\n\\nIf you are defining a type of Secret that's for public use, follow the convention\\nand structure the Secret type to have your domain name before the name, separated\\nby a `/`. For example: `cloud-hosting.example.net/cloud-api-credentials`.\\n\\n### Opaque Secrets\\n\\n`Opaque` is the default Secret type if you don't explicitly specify a type in\\na Secret manifest. This\\nis a legacy mechanism that provides long-lived ServiceAccount credentials to\\nPods.\\n\\nIn Kubernetes v1.22 and later, the recommended approach is to obtain a\\nshort-lived, automatically rotating ServiceAccount token by using the\\n[`TokenRequest`](/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/authentication-resources/token-request-v1/)\\nAPI instead. You can get these short-lived tokens using the following methods:\\n\\n* Call the `TokenRequest` API either directly or by using an API client like\\n  `kubectl`. For example, you can use the\\n  [`kubectl create token`](/docs/reference/generated/kubectl/kubectl-commands#-em-token-em-)\\n  command.\\n* Request a mounted token in a\\n  [projected volume](/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/service-accounts-admin/#bound-service-account-token-volume)\\n  in your Pod manifest. Kubernetes creates the token and mounts it in the Pod.\\n  The token is automatically invalidated when the Pod that it's mounted in is\\n  deleted. For details, see\\n  [Launch a Pod using service account token projection](/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#launch-a-pod-using-service-account-token-projection).\\n\\n{{< note >}}\\nYou should only create a ServiceAccount token Secret\\nif you can't use the `TokenRequest` API to obtain a token,\\nand the security exposure of persisting a non-expiring token credential\\nin a readable API object is acceptable to you. A secondary means of establishing trust is needed to\\nmitigate \\\"man in the middle\\\" attacks, such as a `known_hosts` file added to a ConfigMap.\\n{{< /caution >}}\\n\\n### TLS Secrets\\n\\nThe `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret type is for storing\\na certificate and its associated key that are typically used for TLS.\\n\\nOne common use for TLS Secrets is to configure encryption in transit for\\nan [Ingress](/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/), but you can also use it\\nwith other resources or directly in your workload.\\nWhen using this type of Secret, the `tls.key` and the `tls.crt` key must be provided\\nin the `data` (or `stringData`) field of the Secret configuration, although the API\\nserver doesn't actually validate the values for each key.\\n\\nAs an alternative to using `stringData`, you can use the `data` field to provide\\nthe base64 encoded certificate and private key. The API server\\nverifies if the required keys are set for a Secret of this type.\\n\\nTo create a TLS Secret using `kubectl`, use the `tls` subcommand:\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl create secret tls my-tls-secret \\\\\\n  --cert=path/to/cert/file \\\\\\n  --key=path/to/key/file\\n```\\n\\nThe public/private key pair must exist before hand. When using this Secret type, you will have to specify a\\n`ssh-privatekey` key-value pair in the `data` (or `stringData`) field\\nas the SSH credential to use.\\n\\nThe following manifest is an example of a Secret used for SSH public/private\\nkey authentication:\\n\\n{{% code language=\\\"yaml\\\" file=\\\"secret/ssh-auth-secret.yaml\\\" %}}\\n\\nThe SSH authentication Secret type is provided only for convenience.\\nYou can create an `Opaque` type for credentials used for SSH authentication.\\nHowever, using the defined and public Secret type (`kubernetes.io/ssh-auth`) helps other\\npeople to understand the purpose of your Secret, and sets a convention for what key names\\nto expect.\\nThe Kubernetes API verifies that the required keys are set for a Secret of this type.\\n\\n{{< caution >}}\\nSSH private keys do not establish trusted communication between an SSH client and\\nhost server on their own. A secondary means of establishing trust is needed to\\nmitigate \\\"man in the middle\\\" attacks, such as a `known_hosts` file added to a ConfigMap.\\n{{< /caution >}}\\n\\n### TLS Secrets\\n\\nThe `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret type is for storing\\na certificate and its associated key that are typically used for TLS.\\n\\nOne common use for TLS Secrets is to configure encryption in transit for\\nan [Ingress](/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/), but you can also use it\\nwith other resources or directly in your workload.\\nWhen using this type of Secret, the `tls.key` and the `tls.crt` key must be provided\\nin the `data` (or `stringData`) field of the Secret configuration, although the API\\nserver doesn't actually validate the values for each key.\\n\\nAs an alternative to using `stringData`, you can use the `data` field to provide\\nthe base64 encoded certificate and private key. For details, see\\n[Constraints on Secret names and data](#restriction-names-data).\\n\\nThe following YAML contains an example config for a TLS Secret:\\n\\n{{% code language=\\\"yaml\\\" file=\\\"secret/tls-auth-secret.yaml\\\" %}}\\n\\nThe TLS Secret type is provided only for convenience.\\nYou can create an `Opaque` type for credentials used for TLS authentication.\\nHowever, using the defined and public Secret type (`kubernetes.io/tls`)\\nhelps ensure the consistency of Secret format in your project. The API server\\nverifies if the required keys are set for a Secret of this type.\\n\\nTo create a TLS Secret using `kubectl`, use the `tls` subcommand:\\n\\n```shell\\nkubectl create secret tls my-tls-secret \\\\\\n  --cert=path/to/cert/file \\\\\\n  --key=path/to/key/file\\n```\\n\\nThe public/private key pair must exist before hand. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EifdkBrS9it8H71wPFxFPh","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t{\n2\t \"files\": {\n3\t  \"after\": \"after.md\",\n4\t  \"before\": \"before.md\"\n5\t },\n6\t \"mechanism_target\": \"### Conflict resolution\\n\\nA conflict happens when you change the same file on two or more devices before they sync. For example, you edit a note on your computer. Before that change uploads, you also change the same note on your phone.\\n\\nConflicts happen more often when you work offline. There are more changes and longer time between syncs, which increases the chance of conflicts.\\n\\n#### How Obsidian Sync handles conflicts\\n\\nWhen Obsidian Sync finds a conflict, the result depends on the file type:\\n\\n- **Markdown files**: Obsidian Sync merges the changes using Google's [diff-match-patch](https://github.com/google/diff-match-patch) algorithm.\\n- **Other file types**: For all other files, including canvases, Obsidian uses a \\\"last modified wins\\\" approach. The most recently modified version replaces earlier versions.\\n\\nFor conflicts in Obsidian settings, such as plugin settings, Obsidian Sync merges the JSON files. It applies keys from the local JSON on top of the remote JSON.\\n\\n#### Conflict resolution options\\n\\nStarting in Obsidian 1.9.7, you can choose how to handle conflicts. To configure this setting:\\n\\n1. Open **[[Settings]]**.\\n2. In the sidebar, select **Sync**.\\n3. Under **[[Sync settings and selective syncing#Conflict resolution|Conflict resolution]]**, choose your preferred option:\\n   - **Automatically merge** (default): Obsidian Sync combines all changes from different devices into a single file. This saves all edits, but it may sometimes create duplicate text or formatting problems. You will need to fix these manually.\\n   - **Create conflict file**: When Obsidian finds conflicting changes, it creates a separate conflict file instead of merging automatically. You can then review both versions and merge them yourself. This gives you full control over the final result.\\n\\n> [!warning]+ Configure on all devices\\n> Conflict resolution settings are device-specific. You must configure your preferred option on each of your devices. This ensures the same behavior across all your synced devices.\\n\\n**Conflict file naming pattern**\\n\\nWhen you use the \\\"Create conflict file\\\" option, Obsidian creates a new file with this naming pattern:\\n\\n```\\noriginal-note-name (Conflicted copy device-name YYYYMMDDHHMM).md\\n```\\n\\nFor example, if a conflict happens in a note called `Meeting notes.md`, the conflict file might be named:\\n\\n```\\nMeeting notes (Conflicted copy MyMacBook2 202411281430).md\\n```\\n\\nThe conflict file contains the changes from the device where the conflict was detected. For example, you edit a note on your computer. Before that change uploads, you also change the same note on your phone.\\n\\nConflicts happen more often when you work offline. There are more changes and longer time between syncs, which increases the chance of conflicts.\\n\\n#### How Obsidian Sync handles conflicts\\n\\nWhen Obsidian Sync finds a conflict, the result depends on the file type:\\n\\n- **Markdown files**: Obsidian Sync merges the changes using Google's [diff-match-patch](https://github.com/google/diff-match-patch) algorithm.\\n- **Other file types**: For all other files, including canvases, Obsidian uses a \\\"last modified wins\\\" approach. The most recently modified version replaces earlier versions.\\n\\nFor conflicts in Obsidian settings, such as plugin settings, Obsidian Sync merges the JSON files. It applies keys from the local JSON on top of the remote JSON.\\n\\n#### Conflict resolution options\\n\\nStarting in Obsidian 1.9.7, you can choose how to handle conflicts. This saves all edits, but it may sometimes create duplicate text or formatting problems. You will need to fix these manually.\\n   - **Create conflict file**: When Obsidian finds conflicting changes, it creates a separate conflict file instead of merging automatically. You can then review both versions and merge them yourself. This gives you full control over the final result.\\n\\n> [!warning]+ Configure on all devices\\n> Conflict resolution settings are device-specific. This ensures the same behavior across all your synced devices.\\n\\n**Conflict file naming pattern**\\n\\nWhen you use the \\\"Create conflict file\\\" option, Obsidian creates a new file with this naming pattern:\\n\\n```\\noriginal-note-name (Conflicted copy device-name YYYYMMDDHHMM).md\\n```\\n\\nFor example, if a conflict happens in a note called `Meeting notes.md`, the conflict file might be named:\\n\\n```\\nMeeting notes (Conflicted copy MyMacBook2 202411281430).md\\n```\\n\\nThe conflict file contains the changes from the device where the conflict was detected. Deleting the node object from\nKubernetes causes all the Pod objects running on the node to be deleted from the apiserver, and frees up their names.\n\nIn version 1.12, `TaintNodesByCondition` feature is promoted to beta，so node lifecycle controller automatically creates \n[taints](/docs/concepts/configuration/taint-and-toleration/) that represent conditions.\nSimilarly the scheduler ignores conditions when considering a Node; instead\nit looks at the Node's taints and a Pod's tolerations.\n\nNow users can choose between the old scheduling model and a new, more flexible scheduling model.\nA Pod that does not have any tolerations gets scheduled according to the old model. But a Pod that \ntolerates the taints of a particular Node can be scheduled on that Node.\n\n{{< caution >}}\n**Caution:** Enabling this feature creates a small delay between the \ntime when a condition is observed and when a taint is created. This delay is usually less than one second, but it can increase the number of Pods that are successfully scheduled but rejected by the kubelet. \n{{< /caution >}}\n\n### Capacity\n\nDescribes the resources available on the node: CPU, memory and the maximum\nnumber of pods that can be scheduled onto the node.\n\n### Info\n\nGeneral information about the node, such as kernel version, Kubernetes version\n(kubelet and kube-proxy version), Docker version (if used), OS name.\nThe information is gathered by Kubelet from the node.","numLines":58,"startLine":45,"totalLines":292}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01H51LASoXMxuHpSgKaScM5y","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
